Every picture, against the words it stands beside

Read straight out of the built chapter, so it cannot go stale behind the book. 10 drawn files and 13 pictures drawn in code, across 32 places. 8 lines have nothing at all to look at. The coded ones are photographed out of the running book, in the state she sees them — they are on a blue-grey card. If a picture does not belong to the words beside it, that is visible here rather than argued about.

b8-chambre.svg

What it is standing beside

Talia opens her eyes.

She stays still for one moment.

Then she remembers.

Switzerland.

Seven days.

Only seven days until the trip.

Talia sits up quickly.

Then her body tells her something else.

She needs to do a pipi.

Talia gets out of bed and goes straight to the bathroom.

Mommy is walking past her bedroom door.

Mommy says, Good morning Talia. Bonjour Talia.

Talia answers, Good morning Mommy. Bonjour Maman !

Mommy smiles. It is morning. C’est le matin.

Talia nods. And I need to do a pipi.

She goes into the bathroom and sits on the toilet.

She does her pipi.

Talia looks at Mommy.

I did my pipi in the toilet. J’ai fait pipi aux toilettes.

Mommy says, Well done! Bravo !

Talia flushes the toilet and washes her hands.

I wash my hands. Je me lave les mains.

alt: Talia waking up in her bed
b8-dents.svg

What it is standing beside

Now she picks up her toothbrush.

The toothbrush. La brosse à dents.

She brushes the front teeth, the back teeth, the top teeth and the bottom teeth.

Mommy asks, Are you finished? Tu as fini ?

Talia brushes two more teeth.

Now I’m finished. Maintenant, j’ai fini.

She rinses her mouth.

Then she remembers the most important question of the morning.

How many days? Combien de jours ?

Mommy holds up seven fingers.

Seven days until Switzerland. Sept jours avant la Suisse.

Talia touches each finger and counts in French.

Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept.

Seven! Sept !

Talia goes back to her bedroom.

alt: Talia brushing her teeth
b8-habille.svg

What it is standing beside

Her school uniform is ready on the chair.

She gets dressed.

My uniform. Mon uniforme.

Mommy says, Yes. Your uniform. Oui. Ton uniforme.

alt: Talia dressed in her uniform
b8-cheveux.svg

What it is standing beside

Talia stands in front of the mirror and brushes her hair.

One piece of hair sticks up.

She brushes it down.

It comes back up.

She brushes it again.

It comes back up again.

Talia points at it.

No!

Mommy laughs.

Talia laughs too.

Mommy helps her with the back of her hair.

Talia says, Thank you Mommy. Merci Maman.

Mommy answers, You’re welcome. De rien.

Talia sits on the bed and puts on her socks.

My socks. Mes chaussettes.

Then she puts on her shoes.

My shoes. Mes chaussures.

Mommy asks, Are you ready? Tu es prête ?

Talia checks herself.

Uniform. Hair. Socks. Shoes.

Yes. I’m ready. Oui. Je suis prête.

Before they go downstairs, Mommy asks, Do you need another pipi?

Talia stops and checks her body.

No. Not now.

Mommy nods. Okay.

alt: Talia brushing her hair
b8-table.petit-dejeuner.svg

What it is standing beside

Papa is already at the breakfast table.

Good morning Talia. Bonjour Talia.

Talia runs to him.

Good morning Papa! Bonjour Papa.

Papa gives her a kiss.

Talia climbs onto her chair.

alt: Talia, Mommy and Papa at the breakfast table
b8-petit-dejeuner.svg

What it is standing beside

Breakfast is ready.

There are eggs, avocado, cucumber and tomatoes.

There are strawberries, banana and apple.

Everything on Talia’s plate is whole food and dairy-free.

Mommy puts eggs and avocado on her plate.

Papa puts strawberries beside them.

Talia points.

The strawberries, please. Les fraises, s’il te plaît.

Papa gives her two more.

Thank you Papa. Merci Papa.

You’re welcome. De rien.

Talia eats one strawberry.

Then she looks at Mommy.

Then at Papa.

Switzerland! La Suisse !

Papa laughs. I knew we were going to talk about Switzerland.

Talia asks, How many days? Combien de jours ?

Mommy answers, Seven days. Sept jours.

Talia holds up seven fingers again.

Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept.

Papa asks, Why are we practising French before the trip?

Talia knows.

Because people there speak French.

Mommy says, Yes. In the part of Switzerland we are visiting, you will hear people speaking French.

Talia smiles.

And I can speak French too.

Papa nods. A little more every day.

Talia says, Good morning. Bonjour.

Then, Thank you. Merci.

Then, Please. S’il te plaît.

Mommy says, Well done! Bravo !

drawn in code · calendrier

What it is standing beside

Mommy brings Talia’s special Switzerland calendar to the table.

There are seven days on it.

One day for today, and six more after it.

Mommy points to the first day.

Today is Monday. Aujourd’hui, c’est lundi.

Talia looks at the word.

Monday. Lundi.

Papa says it too.

Monday. Lundi.

Mommy asks, What day is it today? Quel jour sommes-nous aujourd’hui ?

Talia answers, Today is Monday. Aujourd’hui, c’est lundi.

Mommy says, Very good. Très bien.

Talia presses Monday on the calendar.

A little mark appears beside it.

This is Day One.

Papa asks, And what comes after Monday?

Talia thinks.

Mommy points to the next day.

Tomorrow is Tuesday. Demain, c’est mardi.

Talia repeats, Tuesday. Mardi.

Mommy points back to today.

But today is Monday. Mais aujourd’hui, c’est lundi.

Talia touches Monday again.

Monday. Lundi.

b8-petit-dejeuner.svg

What it is standing beside

There is one more thing we are practising before Switzerland.

Talia knows what she means.

My pipi.

Mommy nods.

Talia and Mommy and Papa have an agreement.

Talia is learning to listen to her body.

When she needs to do a pipi, she goes to the toilet.

She practises in the daytime.

She practises at night too.

Mommy asks, Where does pipi go?

Talia answers, In the toilet. Aux toilettes.

Papa asks, And when your body tells you that you need to go?

Talia says, I go to the toilet. Je vais aux toilettes.

Mommy says, Exactly. Exactement.

Papa says, Even when you are playing.

Even when I am playing.

Even when you are drawing.

Talia looks at him.

Even if it is a very good drawing?

Papa says, Even then.

Even if I am winning a game?

Mommy says, The game can wait for two minutes.

Talia thinks.

Then she says, I go to the toilet. Je vais aux toilettes.

Mommy smiles. Bravo! Bravo !

School. L’école.

Talia jumps down from her chair.

drawn in code · classe

What it is standing beside

Her friends are already in the classroom.

She puts away her school bag.

Then she sees her friends.

Good morning, my friends! Bonjour, mes amis !

One friend comes over.

Talia has news.

I’m going to Switzerland! Je vais en Suisse !

Her friend looks surprised.

When?

Talia holds up seven fingers.

In seven days! Dans sept jours !

She counts them in French.

Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept.

Her friend asks, What are you going to do there?

Talia starts with the best parts.

The airplane. L’avion.

The mountains. Les montagnes.

The train. Le train.

The lake. Le lac.

Her friend asks, Do people speak French there?

Talia nods.

Yes. I am practising.

Then Talia says, Good morning. Bonjour.

Her friend says, Bonjour.

Talia laughs.

The teacher calls the children to sit down.

The class talks about the day.

The teacher asks what day it is.

Talia puts up her hand.

Today is Monday. Aujourd’hui, c’est lundi.

The teacher says, Very good.

Talia whispers to her friend, Monday. Lundi.

Her friend tries it too.

Lundi.

What it is standing beside

Later, it is drawing time.

Talia takes paper and pencils.

She draws a large mountain.

Her friend points at it.

Is it big or small? C’est grand ou c’est petit ?

Talia answers, Big! Grand !

She draws another mountain.

Then she draws a long train.

The train. Le train.

She draws windows in the train.

Then she draws a lake beside the mountains.

The lake. Le lac.

Her friend asks, Where are you?

Talia draws herself beside the train.

Then Mommy.

Then Papa.

Then she remembers something.

My suitcase! Ma valise !

She draws a suitcase beside herself.

Her friend says, It is very big.

Talia says, I need my things.

All your toys?

Talia remembers Papa’s words.

Not the whole bedroom.

Both girls laugh.

At playtime, Talia runs outside with her friends.

They run and climb and make up a game.

Talia is busy.

Then her body gives her a message.

Pipi.

Talia stops.

For one moment, she wants to keep playing.

Her friends are running to the other side of the playground.

Then she remembers breakfast.

Even when you are playing.

Talia goes to her teacher.

I need to go to the toilet. J’ai besoin d’aller aux toilettes.

The teacher says, Of course.

Talia goes to the bathroom.

She does her pipi in the toilet.

She flushes and washes her hands.

Then she goes back outside.

Her friends are still there.

The game is still there.

Talia joins them again.

The children listen to a story.

After dinner, Talia goes to the Switzerland calendar.

Monday is almost finished.

Tomorrow is Tuesday. Demain, c’est mardi.

Papa asks the question that belongs to every day of the trip countdown.

How many days? Combien de jours ?

Talia holds up seven fingers.

Today began with seven days.

Talia says, Seven days. Sept jours.

Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept.

Mommy folds one finger down.

When you wake up tomorrow, six days will be left. Demain, il restera six jours.

Talia looks at the six fingers.

Six days. Six jours.

Un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six.

Now it is bedtime.

Talia goes upstairs.

She changes into her pajamas.

My pajamas. Mon pyjama.

Then she goes to the bathroom.

She does not need Mommy to remind her.

I’m going to do a pipi. Je vais faire pipi.

She sits on the toilet and does her pipi.

Then she flushes and washes her hands.

I wash my hands. Je me lave les mains.

What it is standing beside

She picks up her toothbrush.

She brushes her teeth carefully.

drawn in code · nuit

What it is standing beside

Talia climbs into bed.

Papa comes in.

Mommy sits beside her.

Papa asks, What day was today?

Talia answers, Monday. Lundi.

What day is tomorrow?

Tuesday. Mardi.

Mommy asks, Where are we going?

Switzerland! La Suisse !

Papa asks, What will you see?

Talia answers one by one.

The airplane. L’avion.

The mountains. Les montagnes.

The train. Le train.

The lake. Le lac.

Mommy says, And every day before the trip, we practise a little French.

Talia nods.

So I can speak French in Switzerland.

Exactly. Exactement.

Mommy pulls up the blanket.

Then she asks, If your body wakes you because you need a pipi, what do you do?

Talia answers, I go to the toilet. Je vais aux toilettes.

Even at night?

Even at night.

Mommy says, Very good. Très bien.

Papa kisses Talia.

Good night Talia. Bonne nuit Talia !

Talia says, Good night Papa. Bonne nuit Papa.

Mommy kisses her too.

Talia says, Good night Mommy. Bonne nuit Maman !

Mommy walks toward the door.

Talia calls, Wait!

Mommy turns around.

Talia holds up six fingers.

When I wake up...

Talia looks at her six fingers. Six days. Six jours.

Papa asks, And tomorrow is...?

Talia answers, Tuesday. Mardi.

Mommy says, Yes. Oui.

Talia says, Good night. Bonne nuit.

Talia closes her eyes.

Monday is finished.

Tomorrow is Tuesday.

And when Talia wakes up, there will be six days until Switzerland.
